title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 74
paragraphs: Those at the Isthmus were struggling with the labor I have described, since now they were running a race in which their very existence was at stake, and they did not expect any brilliant success from their ships. Those at Salamis, though informed of this work, were still dismayed, fearing not so much for themselves as for the Peloponnese. For a while they spoke of it in private, one man beside another, marveling at Eurybiades's bad counsel; but at last it broke out in public. A meeting was held, and much was said on the same points as before: some argued that they should sail away to the Peloponnese and take the risk in defense of that country, not stay and fight for a land that had already been taken by the enemy, while the Athenians, Aeginetans, and Megarians urged that they remain and defend themselves there.
